source_evidence: In a traditional 401(k) account, employee contributions to a 401(k) plan and any earnings from the investments are tax-deferred. You pay the taxes on contributions and earnings when the savings are withdrawn. In a Roth 401(k) account, employee contributions are not tax-deferred but are made with after-tax dollars. Income earned on the account, from interest, dividends, or capital gains, and withdrawals are generally tax-free.
answer: Traditional and Roth 401(k) accounts differ in when their tax benefits apply. With a traditional 401(k), contributions and investment earnings are tax-deferred, and taxes are paid when the savings are withdrawn. With a Roth 401(k), contributions are made with after-tax dollars, while account earnings and withdrawals are generally tax-free. A plan may let you allocate money to either option or to both.
